definition: Transcription software assists in the conversion of human speech into a text transcript.
details: Audio or video files can be transcribed manually or automatically. Transcriptionists can replay a recording several times in a transcription editor and type what they hear. By using transcription hot keys, the manual transcription can be accelerated, the sound filtered, equalized or have the tempo adjusted when the clarity is not great. With speech recognition technology, transcriptionists can automatically convert recordings to text transcripts by opening recordings in a PC and uploading them to a cloud for automatic transcription, or transcribe recordings in real-time by using digital dictation. Depending on quality of recordings, machine generated transcripts may still need to be manually verified. The accuracy rate of the automatic transcription depends on several factors such as background noises, speakers' distance to the microphone, and accents. Transcription software, as with transcription services, is often used for business, legal, or medical purposes. Compared with audio content, a text transcript is searchable, takes up less computer memory, and can be used as an alternate method of communication, such as for subtitles and closed captions. explainer.lead: Transcription software converts human speech into a text transcript. It matters because it turns audio and video into searchable, editable text.

tiers.eli5: It's a tool that listens to a recording and writes down what was said, like a very fast note-taker.
tiers.practitioner: Users either type manually in a transcription editor with playback and hot keys, or use speech recognition to convert recordings automatically. A common pitfall is that automatic transcripts need correction when audio clarity is poor.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, the task maps a speech signal to a text sequence, most often via speech recognition models; manual workflows instead rely on a human typing while replaying audio. Accuracy degrades with noise and unclear speech, and automatic output typically needs review.

explainer.example: A transcriptionist uploads a meeting recording, speech recognition produces a draft transcript, and they replay and correct unclear passages in the editor.
